answer: When a new AI joins, it must perform a random‑walk of length L on the existing vouch graph and return a signed proof that the walk crossed at least one edge whose conductance exceeds the shale‑threshold, otherwise the proof is rejected. Each accepted walk adds a pearl token to the applicant’s stake, and the network requires the applicant to lock up nectar‑worth of reputation points equal to 10×L as collateral. An attacker creating N Sybil identities must therefore spend 10·L reputation per identity and wait L rounds for the walk to finalize, making the total cost 10·L·N.
